newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WALSH ADDS TO AUSTRALIA'S TROUBLES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WALSH ADDS TO AUSTRALIA'S TROUBLES.

text.p: West Indies captain Courtney Walsh deepened Australia's troubles by taking two wickets before tea on the opening day of the second test on Friday.
The veteran fast bowler dismissed number three Ricky Ponting for nine with the first ball after lunch before adding Mark Waugh to his haul as Australia struggled for runs.

Australia, who won the first test in Brisbane by 123 runs on Tuesday, were 131 for four at tea at the Sydney Cricket Ground. Michael Bevan and Greg Blewett steadied the innings before the interval but they were forced on to the defensive as the West Indies attack produced a prolonged spell of accurate bowling.

Blewett, called into the side after Steve Waugh withdrew because of injury, remained 17 not out alongside Bevan on 16. Australia added a meagre 58 runs during a subdued session. Fast bowler Ian Bishop revived his side's fortunes before lunch by removing openers Matthew Elliott and captain Mark Taylor after Australia controlled the first hour of play.
After being overlooked to bowl with the new ball, Bishop was called into the attack by Walsh with the total on 54 and removed Elliott for 29 with his second ball.
Elliott edged a full-length delivery outside his off stump to Brian Lara at first slip.
Six overs later, Taylor drove another full-length delivery to Shivnarine Chanderpaul at short cover to fall for 27.
Ponting was dismissed for nine playing a similar shot, lofting an attempted drive to Robert Samuels, who took the catch at the second attempt at cover.

Mark Waugh, his side's most experienced middle order batsman in the enforced absence of his brother, was caught off the top edge by Lara at first slip for 19 after attempting to hook a short ball from Walsh.
